task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 31, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style newspaper explainer about the Corven Trades Partnership, answering what paid training covers and what apprentices still need to budget for.

facts.text: The Corven Trades Partnership enrolled its first 24 maintenance apprentices in August 2026 under agreements with eight local employers.
A normal full week consists of four eight-hour workplace days and one eight-hour college day.
Both workplace and scheduled classroom hours are paid at an initial $16 an hour, giving $640 gross for a full 40-hour week.
The quoted gross pay is before individual tax or other deductions, which are not supplied.
Annual tuition is $3,600 per apprentice, funded by $2,400 from the partnership grant and $1,200 from the employer.
Apprentices are not billed that tuition under the current agreement, but commuting and ordinary meals are not covered.
The required personal tool kit costs $240, with reimbursement offered after six months of continued participation.
The tool reimbursement is not available in cash before the kit is purchased.
A rise to $18 an hour requires both completion of specified assessments and employer confirmation of listed workplace competencies.
Eighteen months is the planned point for that review, not an automatic calendar-based pay rise regardless of completion.
The apprenticeship runs for two years, while employment beyond that period depends on the individual employer's plans and agreement.
Apprentice Sora Reed previously worked retail shifts and says losing a day's wages to attend college would have prevented her joining.
Reed said, "I can plan around a paid class day. I could not replace that day's wages with a certificate."
Employer representative Deni Holt says apprentices are productive workers but need time from experienced staff for supervision.
Holt said, "Paying the learner is one cost. Making time for the person teaching them is another."
The grant covers this enrolled cohort and does not yet fund another intake.
Attendance requirements and arrangements for missed class days are set out in each apprentice's supplied program agreement, not replaced by an unlimited paid-study entitlement.
The partnership has no completion or post-program earnings outcomes yet because this is its first cohort.
Training takes place in a renovated college workshop that also serves existing evening courses.
The program's first cohort includes adults changing careers as well as recent school leavers; prior jobs include retail, warehousing and office administration.

forbidden_additions: $640 take-home pay, all living costs covered or immediate tool-reimbursement cash
